lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.p450GroundEnergy_correctness
lean.plain: Energy error of the compiled circuit
lean.annotation: `thcHamiltonian dfthc` uses the rounded factors. Each group of 14 squares shares 29 orbital vectors. Expanding the squares puts the linear terms in `h1eMod` and quadratic terms in `zeta`. The printed right-hand side of Eq. (18) also contains the constant $\frac12\sum_{r,c}(W^{(rc)})^2$, about 118.728 Ha. Lean subtracts it and uses the resulting energy convention for the bounds and decoder.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450.dfthc
lean.plain: From the DFTHC factors to the THC matrix
lean.annotation: Lean encodes the fixed model as a rank-261 THC factorization for 58 spatial orbitals: `chi` is `leafVector`, and `zeta` sums the outer products of the 126 fragment vectors. In `h1eMod`, each leaf projector gets the sum of its fragment coefficients weighted by the corresponding shifts, with a plus sign; the other term is a weighted sum of one-body outer products that does not require an orthonormal eigenbasis.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.BlockEncodingCore.p450HBlocked
lean.plain: An exact change in the ordering of the spin orbitals
lean.annotation: `p450HBlocked` is the fixed DFTHC Hamiltonian written in spin-blocked order: it is defined as $UH_{\mathrm{DFTHC}}U^\dagger$, where $U$ is the fermionic-swap uninterleaving unitary. This exact change of basis preserves eigenvalues and is distinct from approximating the Hamiltonian implemented by the walk.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.P450.systemQubits
lean.annotation: Qubit $2p+\sigma$ gives the occupation of spin orbital $(p,\sigma)$, so `systemQubits` is $2\times58=116$. The 63-electron projector selects the span of the basis strings with exactly 63 occupied bits. This subspace has dimension $\binom{116}{63}$.

statements.note: Omitted orbitals can contribute enough correlation to change the order of the doublet and quartet. The reported 0.28 mHa difference from fitting the DFTHC factors concerns a correlation-energy calculation. The benchmark fixes the orbital space and factors, so the 1 mHa bound is on the circuit error for that model.
